readme: Timing baselines for scripts/perf-gate.mjs. A key is one machine class, because a
number from a laptop with an RTX 3080 Ti means nothing on a shared GitHub runner.
The metric names and the regexes that produce them live in scripts/perf-gate.mjs.
To seed or re-seed a key: run the measurement command on that machine and pipe it
through `node scripts/perf-gate.mjs --key <key> --seed`, then commit the diff with
the machine described in `machine` and a `source` saying what produced it. A key
that is absent is not a failure - the gate reports it, writes the observed numbers
as an artifact and passes, so the first CI run on a new runner tells you what to
paste back here. The same is true of a metric a key has no value for.
Tolerance, and why the default is not 5%: the x264 p95 measured on the dev box ranged
4405 to 9067 us across runs of the same release binary, entirely according to how many
other rustc processes were on the machine - a 2.06x spread with nothing changed in the
code. A hosted runner is a shared VM and is no quieter. Two things make the gate usable:
perf-gate.mjs takes several --input files and uses the LOWEST reading per metric (the
one least polluted by contention), and the tolerance below is set from the residual
spread of those minima rather than from a wish.
A key may carry its own `tolerance`, which wins over this one. That is how the 5% gate
the overhaul brief asked for is approached without making the CI job flap: an idle dev
box is a tighter instrument than a shared runner, and only it can afford a tighter gate.
Measured on the idle dev box, 2026-09-08, five consecutive runs of the same release
binary: 4157 / 4243 / 4244 / 4261 / 4490 us, an 8.0% spread with nothing changed. So 5%
would fail on noise even there, and 10% is the tightest honest number for a quiescent
machine; the 20% default stays for anything shared. Tighten a key once it has history.

dev-windows-rtx3080ti.machine: Windows 11 build 26200 (25H2), RTX 3080 Ti Laptop + Intel UHD, primary 1920x1080@360
note: This box, not a runner. Kept so a local run has something to compare against, and it
carries its own 10% tolerance because an idle dev box is a tighter instrument than a
shared VM: five consecutive runs of one binary spanned 4157-4490 us (8.0%), so 5% would
flag noise and 10% is the tightest honest gate. Under load the same binary has measured
4405 / 4883 / 5316 / 5787 / 9067 us - only trust this key on a quiescent machine.
x264_wall_ms is deliberately not baselined: it measures machine load rather than the
encoder (805 ms here against the 3334 ms in docs/BASELINE.md, same binary).
windows_capture_to_encoded_* and windows_capture_encode_p95_us are deliberately absent.
The harness that produces them (test/capture_latency.rs) needs DXGI Desktop Duplication,
and on this box every attempt returns DXGI_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED for \.\DISPLAY1 on the only
adapter that enumerates the output - the pre-existing dxgi_duplication_probe fails the
same way, so it is the machine, not the harness. Seed them from a session where
An absent metric is reported and passed, never failed, so leaving them out costs nothing.
